# FDG7045

> DO NOT allow publicly callable APIs to explicitly or implicitly throw `NullReferenceException`, `AccessViolationException`, or `IndexOutOfRangeException`. These exceptions are reserved and thrown by the platform and in most cases indicate a bug.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.3.5 NullReferenceException, IndexOutOfRangeException, and AccessViolationException.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA2201, CA1062
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Library only: the text scopes it to publicly callable APIs. CA2201 reports creating NullReferenceException, AccessViolationException and IndexOutOfRangeException (the explicit case). CA1062 reports a parameter of a public method that is dereferenced without a null check, which the body's argument checking prevents; implicit throws from other sources (an index out of range, a null field) are not seen, so coverage is partial. Neither has a code fix. CA1062 is mapped in chapter 5 too (FDG5108).

## From the book

Do argument checking to avoid throwing these exceptions. Throwing these exceptions exposes implementation details of your method that might change over time.
